items.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: one night I emceed for Miles, one of Miles’s groups... [INTERVIEWER] Cicely Tyson? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. She’s sitting over in the wings.

ctx.x: Yeah, because a lot of cats – like, I was working clubs. Cats were saying, “He’s on it. But what’s that that you’re playing?” They say, “Why don’t you . . . ? – you can’t be hipper than Miles Davis.” Miles was playing what they thought was like rock or something. So I said, aw, Miles, come on. Come back to jazz. Because one night I emceed for Miles, one of Miles’s groups. Boy, they were paying him a lot of money. He made all the money [?], and he’s playing this music. I’m looking at this great man playing this…

Yeah. She’s sitting over in the wings. You know how Miles used to act. He had a different act altogether. He was playing like nursery rhymes [Freeman sings a ditty]. Then he’d smile at her. “Come on, give us some sugar” or something. Then he – and something was wrong with his leg.
